prompt: A company's internal AI-adoption program (rolling out AI copilots across multiple functions) needs a KPI scorecard for the leadership steering committee. Design 4-6 KPIs.
context: Program status: AI copilot tools have been licensed for 4 functions (customer support, sales, finance, engineering). A 60-day pilot in customer support showed 71% of licensed users had logged in at least once, but only 24% were using it weekly by day 60 — a gap flagged internally as "activation without habituation". Leadership's stated goal is measurable productivity impact within 2 quarters, not just tool rollout.

binaryCriteria.description: Includes both an activation metric (e.g., has logged in/tried the tool) and a separate habituation metric (e.g., weekly active use), explicitly citing the pilot's 71%-vs-24% gap as the reason these must be tracked separately.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the scorecard uses a single blended "adoption" metric that does not distinguish activation from ongoing habitual use.

binaryCriteria.description: Presents metrics cut by function (customer support, sales, finance, engineering) rather than only a single company-wide blended figure.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the scorecard is presented as one blended number with no per-function breakdown.

binaryCriteria.description: Includes at least one productivity/outcome-linked metric per function, matching leadership's explicitly stated goal of measurable productivity impact, not just usage/login rates.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the scorecard consists only of usage/login metrics with no productivity-outcome metric.

goldNotes: A strong scorecard distinguishes activation (has logged in / tried the tool) from habituation (ongoing, weekly active use) as two separate metrics, explicitly because the pilot data already showed a large gap between the two (71% vs. 24%) — collapsing these into a single "adoption" number would hide exactly the problem the pilot already surfaced. It should include a per-function cut (customer support, sales, finance, engineering) rather than a single blended adoption number, since rollout timing and use-case fit likely differ by function. Given leadership's explicit goal of measurable productivity impact (not just usage), the scorecard should include at least one outcome/productivity-linked metric per function (e.g., time-per-ticket in customer support, proposal turnaround time in sales) rather than stopping at usage metrics alone — a scorecard that only measures login/usage rates without any productivity-outcome metric would not meet leadership's explicitly stated goal.
